data.title: Bezos Earth Fund awards $100 million-plus in grants to protect the Amazon
data.description:
The Bezos Earth Fund, a philanthropy project started by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez Bezos, on Thursday announced a fresh round of grants totalling over $100 million to help protect the Amazon rainforest.

  • 15 grants will support conservation and protection efforts

  • they aim to protect forests, support Indigenous lands, restore damaged areas, and track the rainforest’s health in real time

  • grants will protect 37 million acres (15 million hectares) of land and improve management of 285 million acres, the fund said, and reduce annual deforestation by roughly 220,000 acres per year

  • Since 2021, the fund has provided $150 million across five countries

data.title: Philly Fed Index Plunges Much More Than Expected In November
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia released a report on Thursday showing regional manufacturing was less widespread in the month of November but continued to expand overall.

The Philly Fed said its diffusion index for current general activity plunged to 6.3 in November after tumbling to 20.9 in October.

While a positive reading still indicates growth, economists had expected the index to show a much more modest decrease to 17.0.

Looking ahead, the Philly Fed said the diffusion index for future general activity crept up to 33.6 in November from 33.0 in October.

data.title: Anthropic shatters record books with $81 billion blockbuster IPO
data.description:
Anthropic raised $81 billion in its blockbuster initial public offering, smashing records and eclipsing SpaceX's June listing to become the largest IPO ever.

The listing comes as IPO activity has cooled since the summer, with volatile market conditions and rising borrowing costs making it harder for companies to secure attractive valuations.

"What's interesting is that demand remains so strong despite broader concerns around AI valuations and spending. It suggests investors are still willing to pay a premium for companies they believe can become long-term leaders in AI," IPOX Vice President Kat Liu said.

A GLANCE AT WORLD'S BIGGEST IPOs

The biggest IPOs globally, ranked by deal size:

ANTHROPIC

Anthropic secured a $1.5 trillion valuation after pricing its blockbuster IPO above the marketed range, underscoring strong investor appetite for the first frontier AI lab to hit Wall Street.

The company, set to debut on the Nasdaq on Thursday, is poised to become the AI industry's benchmark, with rival OpenAI reportedly eyeing a 2027 listing.

Anthropic and certain selling stockholders sold 980 million shares in an upsized IPO at $83 apiece. They had initially marketed 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each.

Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, but expectations came down due to broader AI worries and even $1.5 trillion was being seen as the high end of the range, Reuters previously reported.

Anthropic also secured $26 billion from some of the world's biggest technology companies in a private placement, alongside the IPO, highlighting the increasingly intertwined financial ties underpinning the AI boom.

Alphabet's Google, Nvidia , Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom , Micron Technology , Microsoft and TSMC agreed to participate in the private placement at the IPO price.

Anthropic, founded in 2021 by a team of researchers who left OpenAI after disagreements over ​governance and AI safety, raised $65 billion at a post-money valuation of $965 billion in late ​May.

OPENAI

OpenAI, which operates AI chatbot ChatGPT, revealed in June that it had confidentially filed for a ​US IPO.

The company will not go public in 2026, CEO Sam Altman had said in September, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence that render "unacceptable" even a 10% risk that AI could cause human extinction by decade's end.

OpenAI President Greg Brockman earlier this month said the company now ‌generates the majority of its revenue from enterprise sales and he ​believes it will be ​ready to go public in ⁠2027.

The company has been racing to ramp up fundraising, Reuters has reported, in order to ⁠capitalize ​on its recent ​growth after delaying its IPO plans.

OpenAI has closed ‌on new funding of $11 billion, the initial part of a round ​that values the company ​at $1.25 trillion, Reuters reported earlier this month.

In May, OpenAI fended off an existential court challenge from Elon Musk, simplifying the path for it to proceed with a stock market listing.

"We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company. But it's a complicated set of tradeoffs and this gives us the option to go public sooner if that ends up being best," OpenAI had said in June.

SPACEX

Elon Musk's rocket and satellite maker SpaceX made a historic Nasdaq debut in June, raising a record $75 billion and eclipsing Saudi Aramco's 2019 listing to become the world's largest IPO at the time.

The offering broke with Wall Street convention by setting the price before the investor roadshow, which is typically used to gauge demand and establish a price range. Its proceeds were more than double those of Saudi Aramco's IPO.

SpaceX shares ended their first trading day at $160.95, valuing the company at $2.1 trillion. The stock has since lost momentum, closing at $143.50 on November 18, but remained above its $135 IPO price.

data.title: Trump urges Congress to pass a new farm bill
data.description:
US President Donald Trump urged Republicans in Congress on Thursday to pass a new farm bill before Democrats take control of Congress in January.

"Our Great Farmers and Ranchers NEED and DESERVE certainty ahead of the 2027 planting season because FOOD SECURITY IS NATIONAL SECURITY! Congressional Republican Majorities, YOU MUST PASS A NEW FARM BILL DURING THE REMAINING DAYS OF CONGRESS. FARMERS AND RANCHERS ARE NOT INTERESTED IN FURTHER DELAYS," Trump said in a Truth Social post from Air Force One as he returned from a trip to Asia that included a summit in China.

The US House of Representatives passed its version of a five-year farm bill in April. The long-stalled, sweeping legislation, which funds agricultural and food aid programs, stills need to pass the Senate before it can advance to Trump's desk.

Historically bipartisan, the farm bill has faced hurdles since the prior bill expired in 2023, as Republicans and Democrats in both chambers battle over its provisions, which range from farm subsidies to food stamps.

data.title: Musk pledges higher Tesla output at China plant, Chinese state media says
data.description:
Tesla chief executive Elon Musk said on Thursday the company would continue to increase output at its China factory, according to Yuyuan Tantian, a social media account affiliated with Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

  • Musk made the remarks in a meeting with Ren Hongbin, head of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, Yuyuan Tantian reported

  • Musk visited Tesla's Shanghai plant during his trip to China, where he also attended APEC events in the southern city of Shenzhen, according to a Tesla executive's social media post. It was his first visit to the factory since 2023

  • In the first 10 months of this year, Tesla delivered 810,889 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles from its Shanghai plant, a 21.4% increase from a year earlier

  • The Shanghai factory currently has a vehicle capacity of over 950,000 units per year

  • The plant sources 98% of the parts used in car manufacturing from within China, and exports to markets including Europe, South Korea and Australia

data.title: Kaplan Earns 2027 Military Friendly® Employer Gold and Military Spouse Friendly® Employer Designations
data.description:
Global education company Kaplan has earned the 2027 Military Friendly Employer Gold designation, which recognizes an organization’s commitment, effort, and success in creating sustainable and meaningful benefits for the military community. Kaplan also earned Gold status in 2026 and was recognized as a Military Friendly Employer in 2025. Additionally, Kaplan was designated as a Top 10 2027 Military Spouse Friendly Employer, in recognition of the company’s commitment to creating sustainable and meaningful career paths for veterans, transitioning service members, and military spouses; it earned this honor for 2026, as well.

Scott Kilgore, Chief Customer Officer, Kaplan North America, said:

“Being recognized once again as both a Military Friendly Employer and a Military Spouse Friendly Employer reflects Kaplan’s enduring commitment to supporting veterans, military spouses, and their families. These distinctions are especially meaningful because they recognize the values we strive to uphold every day: service, integrity, opportunity, and respect for the unique experiences and talents of the military community. Veterans and military spouses bring invaluable leadership, resilience, adaptability, and a strong sense of purpose to our organization. As a U.S. Army veteran myself, I’m especially proud that Kaplan continues to foster a workplace where those who have served, and the families who support them, can build rewarding careers, contribute their talents, and thrive.”

Kayla Lopez, vice president of memberships, Military Friendly®, said:

"We salute our members for raising the bar and understanding that hiring military personnel is not an act of goodwill but a testament to a standard that truly embodies sound business wisdom. Their steadfast commitment to integrating military personnel into their workforce not only reflects the Military Friendly® mission but also underscores their business acumen."

The 24th annual list of Military Friendly® Employers has been released on www.militaryfriendly.com and will be published in the December 2026 issue of G.I. Jobs® magazine, recognizing 282 employers.

Contact Russell Schaffer at russell.schaffer@kaplan.com for more information.

About Kaplan

Kaplan, Inc. is a global education company that helps individuals and institutions advance their goals in an ever-changing world. Our broad portfolio of solutions helps students and professionals further their education and careers, universities and educational institutions attract and support students, and businesses maximize employee recruitment, retention, and development. Stanley Kaplan founded our company in 1938 with a mission to expand educational opportunities for students of all backgrounds. Today, our thousands of employees working in 40 countries/regions continue Stanley’s mission as they serve about 1.2 million students and professionals, 17,000 corporate clients, and 1,500 schools, school districts, colleges, and universities worldwide. Kaplan is a subsidiary of the Graham Holdings Company (). Learn more at kaplan.com.

Military Friendly® is the standard that measures an organization’s commitment, effort, and success in creating sustainable and meaningful benefits for the military community. data.title: South African Reserve Bank Maintains Main Repo Rate at 7.25%
data.description:
By Alexandra Wexler

JOHANNESBURG--The South African Reserve Bank maintained its main repo rate at 7.25% on Thursday amid an uncertain global outlook and higher domestic inflation.

SARB Gov. Lesetja Kganyago said South Africa's inflation has been much higher than expected since the start of the year, and growth has been lower with unemployment on the rise.

"Longer-term growth will have to come from rising investment, and not just more consumption. As it stands, fixed investment in South Africa is much too low, at about 13% of output," Kganyago said. "This is well below historical peaks, and also one of the lowest rates in the world."

Headline inflation in South Africa was 5.2% in October, up from 4.5% in September and the highest level since May 2024, mostly attributable to higher fuel prices. In 2025, inflation averaged 3.2%, a 21-year low. The SARB's inflation target is 3%, with a "tolerance band" of plus or minus one percentage point.

The SARB projects GDP growth of 1.2% this year, in line with its September estimate.
